For the triangular profile $f(n)=\max(0,k-n)$ we have $\sum_{n\ge0}f(n)=k(k+1)/2$. A direct check gives  
$$\sum_{i=1}^{20}f(n_i)=\sum_{n_i<k}(k-n_i)\ge 20k-\sum n_i=20k-N,$$
with equality attainable by taking $n_i\in\{k-1,k\}$ (or all $<k$) as needed; hence $g(N)=\max(0,20k-N)$.

The budget $k(k+1)/2\le2016$ forces $k\le63$ (since $63\cdot64/2=2016$). With $k=63$, $20k=1260\le2016$, so
$$\sum_{N=0}^{2016}g(N)=\sum_{N=0}^{1260}(1260-N)=\frac{1260\cdot1261}{2}=794430.$$

Optimality: writing $f(n)=\sum_j\mathbf 1_{n<c_j}$ with $\sum c_j\le2016$ ($c_1\ge c_2\ge\cdots$), one shows by a rearrangement/majorization argument that $\sum g$ is maximized when the $c_j$ are as equal as possible, i.e. $c_j$ form an interval $1,2,\dots,k$, which is exactly the triangular $f$. Any other shape yields a no larger total. Thus the maximum is $794430$.
